title: Maximum sum of k consecutive elements
prompt:
PageTurn wants a "best streak" badge: the highest total reading minutes over any k consecutive days.

Write maxSumOfK(nums, k) that returns the largest sum of any k consecutive elements of nums. If k < 1 or k > nums.length, return null. Aim for O(n) time; adding up every window from scratch is O(n · k).

Examples:

  • maxSumOfK([20, 5, 35, 40, 10, 0, 30], 3) → 85 (35 + 40 + 10)
  • maxSumOfK([-5, -2, -8, -1], 2) → -7 (values can be negative)
  • maxSumOfK([4, 2], 3) → null

Constraints: 0 ≤ nums.length ≤ 105, −104 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 104.

tests.name: k = 1 is the largest element; k = length is the total
all negative values (don't start best at 0)
invalid k returns null
matches adding up every window on many small inputs

hints: "k consecutive" is a fixed-size window. Neighbouring windows share k − 1 elements, so don't re-add them.

Sum the first k elements. Then for each right from k to the end: add nums[right] (entering) and subtract nums[right - k] (leaving). Track the best. Start best at the first window's sum, not 0, so all-negative inputs work.

Shape:

if (k < 1 || k > nums.length) return null;
let windowSum = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) windowSum += nums[i];
let best = windowSum;
for (let right = k; right < nums.length; right++) {
  windowSum += nums[right] - nums[right - k];
  best = Math.max(best, windowSum);
}
return best;
explain:
Time O(n), space O(1). Each element is added once and subtracted once. The brute force is O(n · k) because it re-adds the k − 1 shared elements for every window.

The same running-aggregate idea powers real systems: a moving average on a metrics dashboard, or a sliding-window rate limiter that keeps a running count of requests in the last minute.

In an interview: "It's k consecutive elements, so a fixed window. I keep a running sum, add the element that enters and subtract the one that leaves, so each slide is O(1) and the whole thing is O(n) with O(1) space."
